title: fix: return structured MCP call errors
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #14510.

- Replace managed Responses MCP error strings with HTTP, protocol, and execution error objects defined by the [current OpenAI SDK](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/v3.8.0/src/openai/types/responses/mcp_tool_call_error.py).
- Validate errors with Zod, retain sanitized tool results, and preserve readable Chat rendering and stateless replay. Previously returned string errors are no longer accepted in replay.
- Keep recovery, usage accounting, and top-level request failures unchanged. Network errors carry a simple message, without a synthetic MCP result. No legacy-error compatibility or cause-chain fallbacks.
- Adversarially reviewed against the actual SDK; removed tests for unreachable SDK error codes. All 164 targeted tests, Gen typecheck, and Biome pass after simplification. Updated with main; net production change is 58 lines across three modules.

gist.headline: Errors learn to speak MCP
gist.blurb: Managed MCP calls now return proper structured error objects instead of a string-shaped shrug. Tool failures keep their useful, sanitized context, so the hive can recover and replay without guessing.
gist.summary: Managed Responses MCP tool-call failures now use the current OpenAI SDK's validated HTTP, protocol, and execution error objects instead of string errors, while preserving sanitized results, readable chat output, and stateless replay.
gist.impact: Developers receive typed MCP error data they can reliably inspect and replay, while network failures remain clear top-level messages without invented tool results.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy MCP repair bench: Polli, wearing tiny mechanic goggles, sorts three clearly different error cards labeled HTTP, PROTOCOL, and EXECUTION into a retro terminal that renders them as neat structured blocks. A small code-plant grows beside the terminal to represent reliable replay and recovery; the monitor robot can hold a sanitized tool-result printout.
